result:
**The plan:** The read-only guard hook found a subcommand's real command by skipping leading keywords, assignments and prefix utilities such as `env` and `time`, then treating the first word left as the command. That word was sometimes one the shell itself skips, so the actual command after it went unchecked. Eight recorded bypasses fell into three classes: a leading `{ … }` group or `[[ … ]]` test, zsh's `=cmd` expansion, and assignments the regex missed. Plan 90 set out to close them without letting through any line that was denied before. A glued glob qualifier was left out on purpose and filed as a deferred item.

**The build:** The old skip loop became `_stop_index`, which can start at any position and remembers results. On top of it, the generator `_command_starts` first yields the old candidate, then branches past `{`, past each later `]]`, past words containing `=`, and from words with their leading `=` stripped. The rewritten `_classify_subcommand` runs every candidate through the existing classifiers and denies on the first hit. Because a hook that times out lets the call through, the walk is bounded by four dedupe and memo mechanisms and a 64-candidate cap that fails closed.

**The project:** The guard's denial set can only grow. A sweep of 150,024 real commands found no line that went from denied to allowed and no new false positives. The branch also adds 148 lines of tests, an updated README, and the retired spec and plan. Small accepted costs remain, such as heredoc text tripping the guard. The change goes live on merge through the hook symlink.
